Chapter 3: The Power of Pausing and Observing
You know, in the middle of our hectic daily routines, just stopping for a moment can feel almost impossible. There’s always something else to check off the list, one more urgent thing to handle. But when we’re dealing with tough emotions, the simple act of pausing—even for just a few seconds—can honestly change everything.
Picture this: a manager under constant pressure at work. One afternoon, a team member makes a careless mistake, and that familiar urge to snap comes rushing in. In the past, this manager might’ve raised their voice, leaving everyone tense and regretting it later. But this time, something shifts. The manager feels the anger bubbling up, notices that tightness in their chest, and just... pauses. For a brief moment, they do nothing. They simply breathe and observe what’s happening inside.
The anger doesn’t magically disappear—but it loses some of its grip. Now, the manager can see that wave of emotion passing through. It’s not a command they have to obey. The urge to react starts to soften. Suddenly, there’s a new option: responding with clarity, instead of lashing out.
Most people don’t realize just how powerful this kind of pause can be. It isn’t about pretending to be calm or stuffing those feelings down. It’s about building a little gap between what triggered you and how you respond—a space where you can actually notice what’s going on. In that gap, old patterns start to loosen, and new choices show up.
I once heard from a young artist who used to battle jealousy whenever she saw others succeed. The feeling would pop up out of nowhere, filling her with bitterness and self-doubt. At first, she tried to push it away, but that only made it stronger. Eventually, she learned to pause and simply notice what she was feeling, without judging herself for it. She’d sit quietly, just acknowledging the jealousy as part of her experience, not something to hide from.
Over time, this changed everything for her. The jealousy still showed up sometimes, but it didn’t run the show anymore. She could see it, understand it, and eventually let it go. That little pause became her doorway to self-compassion and real growth.
And here’s the best part: anyone can learn this skill. It starts with tiny moments—taking a breath before jumping in with a response, noticing the urge to interrupt, or feeling that tension rise before an argument. Every pause is a chance to check in, to really see what’s happening inside, and to spot the hook before you’re caught by it.
This isn’t about being passive or uncaring. It’s about choosing how you respond, instead of just running on autopilot. With each pause, you make space for wisdom to show up. Your mind gets clearer, your heart feels more open, and the way forward—well, it’s a lot less reactive.
And here’s something to remember: the more you practice pausing, the easier it gets. Sure, the triggers don’t just disappear. But those knee-jerk reactions lose their urgency. Life stops being all about fighting or running away, and starts being about meeting each moment with curiosity—and a little more kindness to yourself.
